newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Duma head offers compromise spending cut figure.
newsitem.headline: Duma head offers compromise spending cut figure.

text.p: Russia's lower house of parliament, the State Duma, will not approve existing government plans to cut spending, but may be ready for compromise, Duma speaker Gennady Seleznyov said on Thursday.
"If we bargain spending cuts down to 30 trillion roubles we may pass this law," Interfax news agency quoted Seleznyov as saying.

The Duma's budget committee said it would recommend that the chamber reject the spending cuts, which aim to slash almost 110 trillion roubles from figures in the 1997 budget. The Duma is due to vote on the proposals on May 23.
Seleznyov also said the Duma might debate a counter-proposal that the government authorise new cash emissions to deal with the budget crisis.

"These would be the roubles tied to the economy. They should not be converted in dollars and leave the country... Enterprises will get funds and people will receive wages they have been waiting for four or five months," Seleznyov said.
The central bank has already said it will not support the plan, warning that it would trigger hyperinflation.
Yegor Stroyev, the head of the Federation Council upper chamber also warned deputees against hasty economic decisions, referring directly to the proposal to print more money.
The Duma on Wednesday ordered the Audit Chamber to check the government's sequestration plan.

Russian government officials say the Kremlin could find other ways to cut spending if parliament does not approve the plan, but they pointed out that sequestration was a much better and more legal solution.
